deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 13% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 10.2% = 10-year Treasury 5.2% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 83% last year; 110%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 81% (3 years ago 47%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $81 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 84% (3 years ago 38%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $3.2B, up 68% from a year ago — about 1% of the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $6.4B, up 215% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 127% vs quarterly sales up 106% (days to collect 54 → 60). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 110%/yr over 3 years and 69%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 65% vs a 5-year range of 16–65% (median 56%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).

note.headline: NVIDIA at 156.14 on report day after reported CEO exit; hold, no trade

summary.thesis: NVIDIA is a grade-A business priced below every fair-value method, but the price assumes high margins hold, and today's report and a reported leadership change come first.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold, and add only after the report if margins hold. Swing: no trade until the 2026-11-17 report is out.
summary.act_at: Add at 150.22 if margin holds; reassess near 218.73

note.happening: The stock fell 4.12% to 156.14 and is in a downtrend, below its 20-day (195.64), 50-day (213.15) and 200-day (203.75) averages. Quarterly results are due on 2026-11-17. Interim CEO Colette Kress presents them, after Jensen Huang's resignation was reported. NVIDIA announced a board committee to oversee national security and export controls, and U.S. agencies reportedly began investigating partner Megaspeed in 2024.
note.business: The business numbers are strong. Revenue for the last 12 months was 303.0B, up from 165.2B. Quarterly sales growth sped up to 105.85% from 73.21% two quarters earlier. Operating margin rose to 65.21% from 58.09%, and free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) reached 127.0B, up from 72.0B. Two things could change the business itself. First, margin is at the top of its 5-year range (16–65%), and peaks like this often fade. Second, unpaid customer bills grew 127% while sales grew 106%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. Export-control and China headlines (reported) could affect demand if they turn into rules (general knowledge), so they are a business risk and not only a mood risk. The reported CEO exit, the new committee and $946.6M of insider sales outside pre-set plans are governance and sentiment issues. They do not change demand or cash today. Balance sheet risk is low: net cash is 23.2B and liquidity is 56.6B.

worth.text: At 156.14 the stock trades at 19.7 times trailing earnings and 9.9 times next year's expected earnings. Price-to-sales (P/S, price divided by yearly sales) is 12.4, below the peer median of 15.7 and at the 4.0th percentile of its own 5-year history. The discounted cash flow (DCF) model, which values future cash in today's money, gives 189.87 / 220.46 / 261.33 (bear / base / bull). Own-history P/S gives 217.35 to 411.04. The current price assumes free cash flow starts growing about 21.0% a year. At 20% starting growth the value is 150.22, and at 30% it is 218.73. So the gap between methods depends mostly on how fast cash flow grows at the start. Margin matters just as much: if operating margin falls to 48% the value drops to 112.91, and at 32% to 75.59. The stock looks cheap only if today's margin holds.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing 20–30% a year and operating margin stays near 65.21% rather than fading toward 48%.

Operating margin of 65.21% is at the top of its 5-year range. At 48% the cash-flow value falls to 112.91, well below the price.

After the report, compare revenue with 108.7B, EPS with 2.47 and next-quarter guidance with 124.9B before acting at 150.22 or 218.73.
